title: Design System: Muhammad Yasir Khan — Portfolio

signal.purpose: The running state and the primary action. Never decoration.

signal-deep.purpose: Orange-tinted shadow spread and hover/error text. Never a fill.

signal-wash.purpose: Region tint for a current / failed callout, always with a signal border and a text label.

success.purpose: The completed state. Re-stepped up from #0f7a4f, which sat at protan deltaE 6.4 against the signal orange; #0a6b45 clears all six palette checks at 9.1. Do not step it back.

success-wash.purpose: Bordered confirmation region on the contact form only.

queued.purpose: The not-yet-reached state. Only ever a 1px outline around a hollow square, plus the inactive carousel dot and the input hover border.

canvas.purpose: Page ground and theme-color. Carries the fixed 26px dot grid, and is the text colour on ink-filled surfaces.

canvas-deep.purpose: The disabled-button ground. Declared once and used once, deliberately.

panel.purpose: Every node, card, figure, icon button and modal surface. Warm-white against the cool canvas.

panel-sunk.purpose: Recessed regions inside a panel: image wells, input fields, bar tracks, row hover. Never gets a shadow.

ink.purpose: Primary text, structural borders on active and heading rules, the footer ground, and the fill behind task ids.

ink-2.purpose: Body copy (set by .t-body), secondary labels, icon rest state.

ink-3.purpose: Meta, counters, captions, axis labels. Raised from #6b7178, which measured 4.12:1 on the canvas; used at 10-11px, so it holds 5.18:1 on canvas and 5.64:1 on the sunk panel. Do not lighten without re-measuring against both grounds.

rule.purpose: Divides a node from the canvas and a node's header from its body.

rule-soft.purpose: Divides repeated rows within a node, and paints gridlines behind measured bars.

display.purpose: The hero h1 only, one per page. Archivo pushed to wdth 118 — the width axis is what gives this world its signage register, not extra weight.

section.purpose: Every node h2 and reduced-clamp sub-headings inside a node. wdth 112.

card-title.purpose: Every h3 inside a node — project titles, company names, figure captions, modal titles. Archivo at default width; the width axis stops at the section level.

body.purpose: All prose. The 68ch measure and the ink-2 colour are part of the token, not applied per-instance.

body-sm.purpose: Secondary prose in dense nodes — modal descriptions, role bullets, form inputs.

body-compact.purpose: The densest prose step — project-card summaries, executor descriptions, gantt company labels, block sub-headings, skill names, form status lines. The floor for card copy and table cells.

caption.purpose: The two micro strings that are prose rather than machine data (the carousel hint, the modal "Built with" label). Deliberately not .t-mono, which is reserved for ids, tags, states and tabular figures.

control.purpose: Every button, filter, tab and nav item. Archivo at wdth 104 / 650 / uppercase — mono is reserved for machine data, and a button set in mono is the costume version of this world.

mono.purpose: Task ids, counters, categories, durations, axis labels. Tabular figures.

mono-label.purpose: State words, section micro-labels (stdout, operator, Graph), form field labels.

shadows.name: node-rest
shadows.purpose: Every .node. A 1px contact shadow plus a wide, tightly-spread ambient lift — always paired with a 1px border.

shadows.name: node-live
shadows.purpose: The current unit: the running role card and both overlay panels. Darker border AND deeper lift together.

shadows.name: signal-rest
shadows.purpose: Primary button at rest. The lift is tinted with signal-deep so the orange reads as emitting.

shadows.name: signal-hover
shadows.purpose: Primary button hover, paired with translateY(-2px).

shadows.name: signal-active
shadows.purpose: Primary button pressed; the lift collapses and the transform returns to 0.

shadows.name: header-condensed
shadows.purpose: The fixed run header once scrollY > 40. A hard hairline plus an extremely diffuse falloff — separates without appearing to hover.

motion.name: ease-run
motion.purpose: Default easing for entrances, scroll reveals, and state transitions.

motion.name: hero-in
motion.value: 0.9s var(--ease-run) both — translateY(14px) + blur(6px) to rest, staggered 80ms + 110ms per row
motion.purpose: The single authored entrance, on the first viewport only. The only place blur is used in the system. Reused at 0.4s for the modal image swap.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: One shared scroll reveal applied by IntersectionObserver. Carries three safeties: reduced motion, missing IntersectionObserver, and a 2500ms failsafe timer — because .reveal starts at opacity 0.

motion.name: run-pulse
motion.value: 1.6s var(--ease-step) infinite — opacity 1 to 0.35, scale 1 to 0.7
motion.purpose: The running-state indicator, and the only infinite animation on the page. Always bound to a live state.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce clamps all animation/transition to 0.001ms, disables smooth scroll, forces .reveal visible
motion.purpose: The run pre-completes: every node is marked success, stateOf never returns running, and the frame-stepper and carousel autoplay do not start. Nothing is hidden behind motion.

motion.name: edge-flow
motion.purpose: DECLARED BUT UNUSED. Present in src/index.css and not drawn between sections anywhere in the build. Recorded as dead CSS, not as a shipping motion token.

components.name: Signal Button
components.description: The primary action. Solid signal orange with ink text, a hard 1px ink border, and an orange-tinted lift.

narrative.overview:
This surface is a pipeline orchestrator's run view rendered as a portfolio. The page is a canvas — a cool graphite ground (#e9eae4) carrying a fixed 26px dot grid — and everything that matters sits on it as a node: a near-white panel with a hard 1px ink-adjacent rule and a genuine offset-plus-blur lift. Sections are tasks with ids (t1.about … t6.contact), the visitor's scroll is the run, and each of twelve projects is a task that reports shipped. Nothing here is a metaphor applied as decoration; the run state is computed in src/hooks/useRun.ts and drives the header, the graph rail, and every section heading from one source.

The density is that of an instrument panel, not a marketing page. Hairlines are the primary structural device — a 1px rule separates almost every row of information, and headings sit on a full-width ink rule. Type does the shouting: Archivo's variable width axis is pushed to 118 for display and 112 for section headings, which gives the world a signage register that more weight alone could not. Martian Mono is confined to machine facts — ids, tags, states, counters, tabular figures. Colour is almost entirely absent until it means something: signal orange and success green are state, not accent.

Two things this refuses on purpose, and the refusals are visible in the build: the near-black terminal hero with a typing animation (the ground here is light, and the only authored entrance is a single 0.9s translate-and-deblur on the first viewport), and its opposite, the whitespace-and-serif minimal resume (there is no serif anywhere, no generous emptiness, and every claim is anchored to a live link or a measured bar).
keyCharacteristics: Light graphite dot-grid canvas under near-white panels — light, not dark; cool, not warm.
Square by default. Radius appears in exactly three places, all functional.
Hairline-led structure: 1px rules do the work that shadows and cards do elsewhere.
Archivo variable pushed on the width axis, not just the weight axis.
Mono is machine voice only, and the boundary is enforced by a separate control role.
Run state is semantic colour + distinct shape + text label, always all three.
One authored entrance, one shared scroll reveal, one state pulse. That is the entire motion budget.

rules.name: The Semantic State Rule
rules.body: Signal orange, success green and queued grey mean running, success and queued. They are never used as decoration, never as a brand accent, and never to differentiate one category of content from another. The one place this was almost broken — the experience timeline — was corrected: those bars carry signal for the current role and success for finished ones, exactly as everywhere else.

rules.name: The Shape-Plus-Label Rule
rules.body: State never travels as colour alone. Every state indicator carries a distinct shape — a pulsing circle for running, a filled square for success, a hollow outlined square for queued — and sits next to a text label (run / ok / —, or running / success / queued). A colour-only status dot is a defect, not a shorthand.

rules.name: The Validated Green Rule
rules.body: --color-success is #0a6b45. It was re-stepped up from #0f7a4f, which sat at protan deltaE 6.4 against the signal orange — inside the confusable band for the most common form of colour-vision deficiency, on a page where orange and green appear side by side in the same legend. #0a6b45 clears all six palette checks at 9.1. Do not step it back toward a brighter green.

rules.name: The Ink-3 Floor Rule
rules.body: --color-ink-3 is #5b616a, raised from #6b7178, which measured 4.12:1 on the canvas. This token is used at 10–11px, so it has to clear the small-text floor with margin: the shipped value holds 5.18:1 on the canvas and 5.64:1 on the sunk panel. Any future lightening must be re-measured against both grounds, not just against white.

rules.name: The Mono Boundary Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono is for ids, tags, states and tabular data. That is the whole list. Controls — buttons, filters, tabs, nav — use .t-control, which is Archivo at wdth 104 / 650 / uppercase. A button set in mono is the costume version of this world; real orchestration UIs do not do it, and neither does this one. This boundary is a rule, not an accident of implementation.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Rule
rules.body: Display presence comes from the width axis (118 → 112 → 104 as the register descends from hero to section to control), not from piling on weight. If a heading needs more presence, widen it before you embolden it.

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose is capped at 68ch by .t-body itself. Never re-cap prose with an ad-hoc max-width utility; use .t-body and let the token hold the measure.

rules.name: The One Container Rule
rules.body: Every top-level region uses max-width 1440px with 20px / 32px gutters. A new section that invents its own width breaks the vertical edge alignment that holds this page together.

rules.name: The Rule-Plus-Lift Rule
rules.body: Every raised surface carries both a 1px border and a blurred shadow. No hard offset shadows (this is not a neobrutalist world), and no borderless drop-shadow cards.

rules.name: The Portal Rule
rules.body: Both overlays — ProjectModal and the testimonial lightbox — are rendered with createPortal into document.body. Every NodeSection is relative z-10, which creates a stacking context; a fixed overlay rendered inside one resolves within that context and paints beneath the z-50 run header. Any future overlay must portal to document.body for the same reason.

rules.name: The Square-By-Default Rule
rules.body: New surfaces get border-radius 0. Radius must be justified as a signal — a focus ring, a value's leading edge, or a running-state circle — never as softening.

rules.name: The Node Reservation Rule
rules.body: .node is reserved for genuine units: a task, a job, a section, a figure, an overlay panel. It is never wrapped around an individual paragraph or list item, and nodes are never nested. If content needs internal separation, use a rule-soft divider or a panel-sunk region, not a second node.

rules.name: The Never-Invisible Rule
rules.body: Any element that starts at opacity 0 must carry a non-observer path to visible. Reveal has three: reduced motion, a missing IntersectionObserver, and a 2500ms failsafe timer. A new entrance animation that can strand content blank is a bug, not a style.

rules.name: The One Entrance Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one authored entrance (hero-in, first viewport) and one shared reveal below the fold. Do not add a second signature entrance for a new section; wrap it in Reveal.

dos: Do run every new section through NodeSection + NodeHeading with a real task id added to the nodes array in src/data/site.ts, so the header, the graph rail and the mobile menu pick it up automatically.
Do pair colour with a distinct shape and a text label for every state indicator — pulsing circle / filled square / hollow outlined square.
Do use .t-control for anything the visitor can press, and reserve .t-mono / .t-mono-label for ids, tags, states and tabular figures.
Do give raised surfaces both a 1px border and a blurred shadow, and use panel-sunk (not a shadow) for recessed regions.
Do portal any new fixed overlay to document.body — sections are relative z-10 and will trap it beneath the z-50 header.
Do wrap below-the-fold content in Reveal rather than authoring a new entrance.
Do cap prose with .t-body, which already holds the 68ch measure and the ink-2 colour.
Do keep object-contain on product screenshots; cropping them destroys the interface evidence that makes the claim credible.
Do re-measure contrast against both canvas (#e9eae4) and panel-sunk (#f2f3ee) before changing any ink token — white is not the ground here.
donts: Don't use signal orange, success green or queued grey for anything that is not run state or a primary action. They are semantic tokens, not an accent palette.
Don't re-step --color-success toward a brighter green. #0f7a4f sat at protan deltaE 6.4 against the signal orange; #0a6b45 is the validated value.
Don't lighten --color-ink-3 past #5b616a — it is used at 10–11px and #6b7178 measured 4.12:1 on the canvas.
Don't set a button, filter, tab or nav item in Martian Mono. That is the costume version of this world.
Don't nest .node inside .node, or wrap .node around a single paragraph. Use a rule-soft divider or a panel-sunk region instead.
Don't add border-radius to a panel, button, input, tag or image. Radius is reserved for the focus ring, the leading edge of a measured bar, and the running-state circle.
Don't introduce a serif, a second sans, or a font loaded from an external CDN. Both faces are self-hosted npm packages, and the Archivo entry point must remain the one carrying the wdth axis.
Don't add blur outside the hero-in entrance and the existing overlay/header backdrop filters.
Don't add a second infinite animation. run-pulse is the only one, and it is bound to a live state.
Don't ship an element that starts hidden without a failsafe path to visible.
Don't hard-code an asset path. The site deploys to the /Portfolio/ subpath; all assets resolve through import.meta.env.BASE_URL.
